title: The pointers that teach the old 64-hex triage still name `ticfac finding` everywhere
body: sg5 replaced the everyday triage path, but every surface that TELLS somebody how to triage still teaches the old one: the `ticfac findings` listing prints `ticfac finding <epic> <64-hex> --promote-as ...`, the run's own findingLeftNote (reconcile/absorb.go) tells workers the same, and the close-out's refusal message names it too. A person or agent following those pointers will type 64-hex keys and create ticks by hand — exactly the friction A3 exists to remove — even though `ticfac triage <epic>` now settles everything by short prefix. The wording lives in reconcile and the findings listing, with tests asserting the old strings, so the change is its own tick rather than part of sg5.
